questions.text: For gabapentin, find instructions for someone whose kidneys remove medicine very slowly and whose blood is cleaned by a machine. Include both the very-low-kidney-function daily-dose rule and the extra dosing associated with a four-hour filtering session.

requirements.description: Proportional reduction below creatinine clearance 15
Maintenance and supplemental post-hemodialysis dosing

references.quote: For patients with creatinine clearance <15 mL/min, reduce daily dose in proportion to creatinine clearance (e.g., patients with a creatinine clearance of 7.5 mL/min should receive one-half the daily dose that patients with a creatinine clearance of 15 mL/min receive).

Patients on hemodialysis should receive maintenance doses based on estimates of creatinine clearance as indicated in the upper portion of the table and a supplemental post-hemodialysis dose administered after each 4 hours of hemodialysis as indicated in the lower portion of the table.

questions.text: In immediate-release metformin labeling, distinguish starting treatment with an eGFR of 38 from managing an existing prescription around iodinated contrast. Find the renal initiation limit, circumstances requiring a temporary hold, and kidney-check and restart conditions after imaging.

requirements.description: Do not initiate at eGFR 30 to 45
Contrast-related hold and qualifying conditions
Recheck after 48 hours and restart only if stable

references.quote: Initiation of metformin hydrochloride tablets in patients with an eGFR between 30 – 45 mL/minute/1.73 m 2 is not recommended.

Discontinue metformin hydrochloride tablets at the time of, or prior to, an iodinated contrast imaging procedure in patients with an eGFR between 30 and 60 mL/min/1.73 m 2 ; in patients with a history of liver disease, alcoholism, or heart failure; or in patients who will be administered intra-arterial iodinated contrast.
Re-evaluate eGFR 48 hours after the imaging procedure; restart metformin hydrochloride tablets if renal function is stable.

questions.text: For clopidogrel and acid-suppressing medicines, locate evidence addressing whether taking omeprazole twelve hours apart removes the interaction, and whether pantoprazole has the same effect. Retrieve the avoidance instruction, the separated-dose finding and the comparison with other proton-pump inhibitors.

requirements.description: Avoid omeprazole or esomeprazole
Reduced activity even twelve hours apart
Other named PPIs had less effect, not an absence-of-risk claim

references.quote: Avoid concomitant use of clopidogrel with omeprazole or esomeprazole.
In clinical studies, omeprazole was shown to reduce significantly the antiplatelet activity of clopidogrel when given concomitantly or 12 hours apart.
Dexlansoprazole, lansoprazole, and pantoprazole had less effect on the antiplatelet activity of clopidogrel than did omeprazole or esomeprazole

limitations: Baseline: 60 original section-finding questions; 20 uses, 20 dosage, 20 warnings.
Challenge: 10 authored questions and 25 required evidence items, frozen before retrieval.
Baseline hits identify a drug section, not a medically sufficient passage.
Hard hits require full coverage of selected source spans; duplicate chunks earn no extra credit.
Exact spans are repository-reviewed anchors, not exhaustive relevance judgments or independent clinical review.
Equivalent wording or other valid evidence can be missed by this strict span-based scorer.
Designed difficulty is not independently validated; ten questions are a small diagnostic stress test.
Existing settings were reused without tuning; all questions are descriptive checks, not an untouched test set.
Timing excludes model loading and API question embedding; no clinical correctness claim follows.
All methods use unfiltered top-10 retrieval without the app parser, score cutoff or answer writer.
